Title: Automatic speech recognition for under-resourced languages: A survey
MethodOrContribution: Narrative survey of challenges, corpora, and multilingual adaptation for under-resourced ASR
LanguageCoverage: Under-resourced languages across pre-2014 ASR literature
MainFinding: Established the canonical problem framing for under-resourced ASR and emphasized multilingual transfer, data creation, and language-specific adaptation.
Limitations: Predates SSL, foundation models, and modern multilingual benchmarks.
UseInReview: Use in the introduction and historical background to show what changed after the pre-foundation-model era.
VerificationStatus: Verified institutional metadata and DOI; publisher page access may be restricted

Title: End-to-End Speech Recognition: A Survey
Venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
MethodOrContribution: Taxonomy survey of CTC, attention, transducer, decoding, and LM integration
MainFinding: Provides a recent field-level taxonomy of end-to-end ASR and clarifies the transition from classical to neural ASR.
Limitations: Broad ASR survey rather than low-resource-specific; limited coverage of post-2024 SpeechLM developments.
UseInReview: Anchor the from-hybrid-to-end-to-end and foundation-model sections and stabilize terminology.

Title: Recent Advances in Speech Language Models: A Survey
MethodOrContribution: Comprehensive survey of SpeechLM architectures, training, evaluation, and open challenges
MainFinding: Best recent survey anchor for the SpeechLM era and a bridge into LLM-assisted speech directions.
Limitations: Not low-resource-specific; examples may age quickly in a fast-moving area.
UseInReview: Use in the foundation-model and LLM-assisted future-directions sections.

Title: Common Voice: A Massively-Multilingual Speech Corpus
MethodOrContribution: Crowdsourced multilingual speech corpus construction with baseline ASR experiments
LanguageCoverage: Massively multilingual crowdsourced speech; 29 released languages at paper time
MainFinding: Established a major public multilingual speech resource that enabled many low-resource ASR baselines.
Limitations: Data quality, demographic balance, and transcript consistency vary by language and release.
UseInReview: Core entry in the dataset table and discussion of crowdsourced resource construction.
VerificationStatus: Verified ACL Anthology URL; no DOI shown on official page

Title: VoxPopuli: A Large-Scale Multilingual Speech Corpus for Representation Learning, Semi-Supervised Learning and Interpretation
MethodOrContribution: Large-scale multilingual speech corpus curation from European Parliament recordings
LanguageCoverage: 400k hours unlabeled in 23 languages; 1.8k hours transcribed in 15 languages
Evaluation: Corpus statistics; SSL and semi-supervised downstream evaluation
MainFinding: Provides a large multilingual unlabeled corpus that became a key pretraining resource for speech representation learning.
Limitations: Domain is formal parliamentary speech and coverage is not optimized for the very lowest-resource languages.
UseInReview: Use in the resource taxonomy to distinguish training corpora from evaluation benchmarks.

Title: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
MethodOrContribution: N-way parallel multilingual benchmark with few-shot baselines
LanguageCoverage: 102 languages; approximately 12 hours supervision per language
Evaluation: ASR; speech language identification; translation; retrieval
MainFinding: Created a reusable parallel benchmark that made multilingual low-resource comparison more standardized.
Limitations: Primarily read speech with fixed prompts; underrepresents spontaneous, noisy, and dialectally rich speech.
UseInReview: Flag as a central benchmark anchor in the resources and evaluation sections.
VerificationStatus: Verified official page plus corroborated DOI

Title: ML-SUPERB: Multilingual Speech Universal PERformance Benchmark
MethodOrContribution: Frozen-feature multilingual benchmark for ASR and language identification
MainFinding: Extended SUPERB beyond English and showed that multilingual SSL benchmarking needs wider language coverage and reproducible protocols.
Limitations: Original setup fixes a shallow downstream model and mostly probes frozen representations.
UseInReview: Use as the first benchmark anchor for multilingual speech foundation-model evaluation.

Title: ML-SUPERB 2.0: Benchmarking Multilingual Speech Models Across Modeling Constraints, Languages, and Datasets
MethodOrContribution: Benchmark extension across downstream architectures, fine-tuning, adapters, LoRA, and supervised models
LanguageCoverage: 142 languages across 15 datasets; about 300 hours total
Evaluation: WER; LID accuracy; robustness across languages and datasets
MainFinding: Shows that benchmark rankings depend strongly on architecture and adaptation setup and that cross-language performance differences remain large.
Limitations: Still constrained by benchmark-scale data budgets and selected task formulations.
UseInReview: Use in adaptation and evaluation sections to connect benchmark design with parameter-efficient tuning choices.
VerificationStatus: Verified ISCA Archive PDF and DOI

Title: The ML-SUPERB 2.0 Challenge: Towards Inclusive ASR Benchmarking for All Language Varieties
MethodOrContribution: Open challenge benchmark with hidden multilingual and dialectal evaluation server
LanguageCoverage: 149 languages and 93 language varieties; 200+ language/variety suite
Evaluation: ASR error rates; robustness and fairness across languages, accents, and dialects
MainFinding: Pushes benchmark design toward inclusive ASR evaluation and shows that strong systems still underperform on accented and dialectal speech.
Limitations: Challenge protocol and hidden-test design are powerful but not a replacement for broad real-world deployment studies.
UseInReview: Anchor the evaluation-beyond-WER discussion, especially dialect and fairness coverage.
VerificationStatus: Verified ISCA Archive PDF and DOI

Title: Data Quality Issues in Multilingual Speech Datasets: The Need for Sociolinguistic Awareness and Proactive Language Planning
MethodOrContribution: Micro- and macro-level quality audit of multilingual speech datasets
DatasetOrBenchmark: Audit of Common Voice 17.0, FLEURS, and VoxPopuli
Evaluation: Dataset quality statistics; transcript, audio, and speech-silence audits
MainFinding: Demonstrates that widely used multilingual speech datasets contain systematic quality problems that affect fair evaluation and reproducibility.
Limitations: Covers three public datasets rather than the full benchmark ecosystem.
UseInReview: Use in critical synthesis to argue that low-resource ASR progress is data-limited and benchmark-sensitive, not only model-limited.

Title: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning: A Review
Venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Topics in Signal Processing
MethodOrContribution: Review of self-supervised speech learning paradigms and downstream implications
MainFinding: Canonical bridge from label scarcity to reusable speech representations.
Limitations: Broader than ASR alone; not low-resource-specific.
UseInReview: Use in SSL/foundation-model precursor section and data-scarcity framing.

Title: A Historical Perspective of Speech Recognition
MethodOrContribution: Historical review of major ASR advances
MainFinding: Useful historical background for pre-SSL and pre-foundation-model framing.
Limitations: Not low-resource-specific.
UseInReview: Use only in historical background and transition from classical to modern ASR.

Title: Speech recognition and keyword spotting for low-resource languages: Babel project research at CUED
MethodOrContribution: Foundational low-resource ASR and KWS program paper grounded in Babel
Evaluation: ASR and KWS under limited/full data
MainFinding: Establishes enduring low-resource bottlenecks and challenge-style evaluation logic.
Limitations: Workshop venue; predates foundation models.
UseInReview: Use in historical benchmark lineage and constrained-data evaluation discussion.

Title: OpenASR20: An Open Challenge for Automatic Speech Recognition of Conversational Telephone Speech in Low-Resource Languages
MethodOrContribution: Open challenge for conversational low-resource telephone speech ASR
MainFinding: Open challenge for realistic low-resource CTS evaluation.
Limitations: Challenge summary rather than broad benchmark family.
UseInReview: Use in evaluation section for realistic constrained CTS benchmarking.

Title: OpenASR21: The Second Open Challenge for Automatic Speech Recognition of Low-Resource Languages
MethodOrContribution: Expanded open challenge with new languages and case-sensitive scoring
MainFinding: Extends open challenge logic with more languages and rigorous scoring.
Limitations: Challenge-oriented, not a broad benchmark family.
UseInReview: Use in evaluation section and benchmark evolution discussion.

Title: SUPERB: Speech Processing Universal PERformance Benchmark
MethodOrContribution: Universal benchmark for speech representation evaluation
MainFinding: Field-defining benchmark design paper that shaped later multilingual benchmarks.
Limitations: Mostly English; not low-resource-specific.
UseInReview: Use as background for benchmark evolution.

Title: XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations
MethodOrContribution: Cross-lingual benchmark for speech representations
MainFinding: Shows the move from generic speech benchmarks to cross-lingual evaluation.
Limitations: Not focused exclusively on ASR or underrepresented languages.
UseInReview: Use as benchmark evolution support.

Title: IndicSUPERB: A Speech Processing Universal Performance Benchmark for Indian Languages
Venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
MethodOrContribution: Regional multilingual benchmark with deeper labeled coverage across speech tasks
MainFinding: Strong example of region-aware benchmark design.
Limitations: Region-specific rather than universal.
UseInReview: Use in regional benchmark and evaluation discussion.

Title: MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research
MethodOrContribution: Large multilingual transcribed corpus with ASR baselines
MainFinding: Strong resource anchor for multilingual ASR scaling.
Limitations: More read-speech than many real-world low-resource settings.
UseInReview: Use in resources/corpora section as major transcribed multilingual corpus.

Title: CMU Wilderness Multilingual Speech Dataset
MethodOrContribution: Multilingual speech dataset release for low-resource experimentation
MainFinding: Useful early multilingual corpus anchor for the transition to modern pretraining corpora.
Limitations: Older and less benchmark-centric than later datasets.
UseInReview: Use as historical multilingual corpus background.

Title: AfriSpeech-200: Pan-African Accented Speech Dataset for Clinical and General Domain ASR
Venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
MethodOrContribution: Pan-African accented English ASR benchmark with public baselines
MainFinding: Makes accent bias and African speech coverage benchmarkable.
Limitations: English-focused.
UseInReview: Use in fairness/accent robustness section.

Title: AfriVox: Probing Multilingual and Accent Robustness of Speech LLMs
MethodOrContribution: Benchmark for multilingual and accent robustness of speech LLMs
LanguageCoverage: 20 African languages plus accented French/Arabic and 100+ African English accents
MainFinding: Best current benchmark bridge between low-resource ASR evaluation and speech LLMs.
Limitations: Very recent; field may move quickly.
UseInReview: Use in LLM-related benchmarking, robustness, and future agenda sections.

Title: FormosanBench: Benchmarking Low-Resource Austronesian Languages in the Era of Large Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Benchmark construction for three endangered Austronesian languages across ASR, MT, and summarization
MainFinding: Useful reserve benchmark exposing how current large models transfer to endangered underrepresented languages.
Limitations: Only three languages and multi-task scope means ASR coverage is narrower than general multilingual benchmarks.
UseInReview: Use as a reserve case box for endangered-language benchmarking and benchmark-tail coverage.

Title: LoASR-Bench: Evaluating Large Speech Language Models on Low-Resource Automatic Speech Recognition Across Language Families
MethodOrContribution: Emerging benchmark for SpeechLM-based ASR across low-resource language families
Evaluation: ASR error rates across languages and scripts
MainFinding: Highly relevant frontier benchmark for speech-LLM low-resource evaluation.
Limitations: Preprint only; metrics and protocol still need peer-reviewed validation and community uptake.
UseInReview: Use in a watchlist box and future-work section.

Title: wav2vec 2.0
MethodOrContribution: Contrastive masked SSL
MainFinding: Established transfer-from-SSL as the modern starting point
Limitations: Mostly English pretraining; needs fine-tuning

Title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
MethodOrContribution: Iterative masked prediction of hidden units
MainFinding: Strong masked-unit SSL baseline; conceptual bridge to later encoders
Limitations: Multilingual low-resource evidence is indirect

Title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
MethodOrContribution: HuBERT-style SSL plus speaker-aware objectives
MainFinding: Stronger universal speech features including speaker cues
Limitations: Venue details and non-English value need careful framing

Title: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-Supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language
MethodOrContribution: Teacher-student latent regression
MainFinding: Important general SSL objective with speech relevance
Limitations: Not a multilingual ASR paper per se

Title: Self-supervised Learning with Random-Projection Quantizer for Speech Recognition
MethodOrContribution: Random-projection quantization targets
MainFinding: Simplifies discrete target generation and improves stability
Limitations: Mostly English evidence

Title: XLS-R: Self-Supervised Cross-Lingual Speech Representation Learning at Scale
MethodOrContribution: Cross-lingual SSL scaled to 128 languages
MainFinding: Core multilingual transfer anchor for low-resource ASR
Limitations: Gains remain coverage- and adaptation-sensitive

Title: mHuBERT-147: A Compact Multilingual HuBERT Model
MethodOrContribution: Compact massively multilingual HuBERT
MainFinding: Strong compact multilingual encoder on open data
Limitations: Encoder-only; downstream ASR still depends on adaptation

Title: AfriHuBERT: A Self-Supervised Speech Representation Model for African Languages
MethodOrContribution: Continued pretraining of mHuBERT on African speech
MainFinding: Shows the value of region-centric continued pretraining
Limitations: Evidence concentrated on African benchmarks

Title: Towards Robust Speech Representation Learning for Thousands of Languages
MethodOrContribution: Robust multilingual SSL at very large linguistic scale
MainFinding: Strong evidence that scaling must be paired with robustness design
Limitations: Less entrenched in ASR practice than Whisper or XLS-R

Title: Scaling Speech Technology to 1,000+ Languages
MethodOrContribution: wav2vec-based SSL plus massively multilingual ASR/TTS/LID
MainFinding: Landmark coverage expansion with strong low-resource transfer
Limitations: Data provenance and domain skew require explicit discussion

Title: Google USM: Scaling Automatic Speech Recognition Beyond 100 Languages
MethodOrContribution: 12M h multilingual encoder pretraining plus supervised ASR
MainFinding: Important scaling-law anchor for multilingual ASR
Limitations: Less reproducible; still preprint-led in public record

Title: SpeechT5: Unified-Modal Encoder-Decoder Pre-Training for Spoken Language Processing
MethodOrContribution: Unified encoder-decoder plus cross-modal pretraining
MainFinding: Early strong bridge between speech and text pretraining
Limitations: Not primarily a multilingual low-resource ASR model

Title: SpeechLM: Enhanced Speech Pre-Training with Unpaired Textual Data
MethodOrContribution: Align speech and text through unified discrete units
MainFinding: Stronger linguistic priors without paired speech-text at scale
Limitations: Low-resource multilingual ASR evidence remains limited

Title: Mu2SLAM: Multitask, Multilingual Speech and Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Joint pretraining on speech, text, ASR, AST, and MT
MainFinding: Important multilingual speech-language bridge
Limitations: More often cited in ST than mainstream ASR practice

Title: Textually Pretrained Speech Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Warm-start speech LM from text LM
MainFinding: Strong evidence that text pretraining transfers into spoken modeling
Limitations: Indirect ASR value; not an ASR benchmark paper

Title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
MethodOrContribution: 680k h multilingual weak supervision
MainFinding: Practical zero-shot baseline that re-centered the field
Limitations: Hallucination and tail-language variability remain material

Title: Joint Speech and Text Machine Translation for up to 100 Languages
MethodOrContribution: Unified multimodal multilingual translation/ASR
MainFinding: Important all-in-one multilingual speech-text foundation model
Limitations: ASR evidence must be separated from ST/TT evidence

Title: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
MethodOrContribution: Data scaling plus data cleaning for open Whisper-style training
MainFinding: Strong reproducibility-oriented open counterpoint to Whisper
Limitations: Still not a universal replacement for strongest industrial systems

Title: OpusLM: A Family of Open Unified Speech Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Family of open unified speech language models
MainFinding: Useful open SpeechLM anchor for AIR
Limitations: Evidence still early relative to ASR-specialized families

Title: Omnilingual ASR: Open-Source Multilingual Speech Recognition for 1600+ Languages
MethodOrContribution: SSL scaling plus LLM-inspired decoder for extensibility
MainFinding: Major long-tail language coverage story for the review
Limitations: Preprint; broad claims need independent replication

Title: Seed-ASR: Understanding Diverse Speech and Contexts with LLM-based Speech Recognition
MethodOrContribution: Audio-conditioned LLM with contextual inputs
MainFinding: Clear example of the LLM-decoder turn in ASR
Limitations: Open reproducibility remains limited

Title: Qwen-Audio: Advancing Universal Audio Understanding via Unified Large-Scale Audio-Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Unified multi-task audio-language pretraining
MainFinding: Useful bridge from audio-language models to SpeechLMs
Limitations: ASR is only a subset of its scope

Title: Qwen2-Audio Technical Report
MethodOrContribution: Natural-language prompt-based audio interaction
MainFinding: Strong open SpeechLM reference point
Limitations: Low-resource ASR evidence is indirect

Title: Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report
MethodOrContribution: Thinker-Talker end-to-end streaming omni model
MainFinding: Important architecture for speech-native multimodal modeling
Limitations: Low-resource ASR validation remains thin

Title: LLaMA-Omni 2: LLM-based Real-time Spoken Chatbot with Autoregressive Streaming Speech Synthesis
MethodOrContribution: Streaming speech decoder on top of Qwen backbone
MainFinding: Strong peer-reviewed SpeechLM anchor
Limitations: Benchmarks lean dialogue-centric more than LR-ASR-centric

Title: Speechless: Speech Instruction Training Without Speech for Low Resource Languages
MethodOrContribution: Text plus duration to audio-token pipeline for scarce-speech tuning
MainFinding: Directly relevant to scarce-speech adaptation
Limitations: Still early and not a broad ASR benchmark paper

Title: Qwen3-ASR Technical Report
MethodOrContribution: Multilingual ASR family plus LLM-based alignment
MainFinding: Strong 2026 ASR-specific watchlist model
Limitations: Preprint; still narrower than MMS or Omnilingual in coverage

Title: Probing Multilingual and Accent Robustness of Speech LLMs
MethodOrContribution: AfriVox benchmark plus targeted PEFT of Qwen2.5-Omni
MainFinding: Shows support gaps and large PEFT gains for unsupported languages
Limitations: Regional benchmark; not universal

Title: LoASR-Bench: Evaluating Large Speech Language Models on Low-Resource Automatic Speech Recognition Across Language Families
MethodOrContribution: 25-language family-aware low-resource ASR benchmark
MainFinding: Reveals script and family effects and language-ID dependence
Limitations: Preprint; benchmark maturity pending

Title: Multimodal In-context Learning for ASR of Low-resource Languages
MethodOrContribution: MICL with speech LLMs plus hybrid hypothesis selection
MainFinding: Valuable 2026 signal that SpeechLMs alone remain weak on unseen LR ASR; hybrid reranking helps
Limitations: Small language set; preprint

Title: vq-wav2vec: Self-Supervised Learning of Discrete Speech Representations
MethodOrContribution: Discrete unit discovery with wav2vec-style self-supervision
MainFinding: Established the discrete-unit lineage later used by HuBERT and w2v-BERT-style speech pretraining.
Limitations: Less multilingual and less scalable than later encoders.
UseInReview: Historical precursor for the SSL-to-foundation transition.

Title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations
MethodOrContribution: Masked latent prediction with contrastive learning on raw waveform
MainFinding: Canonical turning point showing near-supervised ASR with very limited labels after SSL pretraining.
Limitations: Primarily monolingual; later multilingual scaling papers are needed for low-resource cross-lingual claims.
UseInReview: Core anchor for the foundation-model transition.

Title: Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning for Speech Recognition
MethodOrContribution: Joint multilingual wav2vec-style pretraining over shared discrete space
MainFinding: Showed multilingual pretraining can outperform monolingual SSL and share representations across languages.
Limitations: Scale is much smaller than later multilingual foundation models.
UseInReview: Anchor the first multilingual-transfer wave.

Title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
MethodOrContribution: Offline clustering + masked prediction over hidden units
MainFinding: Replaced contrastive targets with hidden-unit prediction and became one of the most influential SSL baselines for ASR transfer.
Limitations: Mostly English-centric in original evaluation; multilingual claims require downstream studies.
UseInReview: Core SSL anchor and comparator in Block B.

Title: W2v-BERT: Combining Contrastive Learning and Masked Language Modeling for Self-Supervised Speech Pre-Training
MethodOrContribution: End-to-end combination of contrastive learning and MLM-style masked prediction
MainFinding: Strong SSL hybrid that reduced dependence on iterative reclustering and pushed encoder quality forward.
Limitations: Venue metadata is less easily verifiable from primary web access than NeurIPS or PMLR items.
UseInReview: Useful bridge between HuBERT and later W2v-BERT 2.0 / Seamless systems.

Title: Self-supervised Learning with Random-Projection Quantizer for Speech Recognition
MethodOrContribution: Random-projection quantization for simpler SSL speech targets
MainFinding: Demonstrated a simpler, effective alternative to learned quantizers and became important in scalable ASR SSL recipes.
Limitations: Reproducibility can vary with random projection initialization.
UseInReview: Use as the efficiency counterpoint to HuBERT and w2v-BERT.

Title: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language
MethodOrContribution: Latent-target self-distillation across modalities
LanguageCoverage: Speech, vision, language; speech evaluated on standard ASR benchmarks
MainFinding: Important because it generalized the SSL target design beyond modality-specific discrete labels.
Limitations: Not speech-only; low-resource ASR evidence is indirect unless paired with downstream papers.
UseInReview: Use to show the abstraction shift from speech-only SSL to general foundation pretraining.

Title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
MethodOrContribution: SSL with masked speech prediction plus denoising and gated relative position bias
MainFinding: Became the strongest full-stack SSL baseline, especially persuasive when arguing that pretrained encoders encode more than phonetic content.
Limitations: Still an encoder requiring adaptation; multilingual low-resource coverage is not the main design axis.
UseInReview: Core comparator for robustness-oriented speech encoders.

Title: XLS-R: Self-supervised Cross-lingual Speech Representation Learning at Scale
MethodOrContribution: Scale multilingual wav2vec-style pretraining to 128 languages and 436k hours
LanguageCoverage: BABEL; Common Voice; CoVoST-2; VoxLingua107; 128 languages
MainFinding: One of the strongest direct pieces of evidence that multilingual scale especially helps low- and mid-resource languages.
Limitations: Still mostly benchmark-driven; does not eliminate language-tail performance gaps.
UseInReview: Central anchor for the multilingual-scaling section.

Title: SpeechT5: Unified-Modal Encoder-Decoder Pre-Training for Spoken Language Processing
MethodOrContribution: Unified encoder-decoder pretraining over speech and text
MainFinding: Important unified speech-text precursor to later SpeechLM and SpeechLLM work.
Limitations: More general spoken-language processing than low-resource ASR specifically.
UseInReview: Use as first major speech-text foundation-model bridge.

Title: SpeechUT: Bridging Speech and Text with Hidden-Unit for Encoder-Decoder Based Speech-Text Pre-training
MethodOrContribution: Hidden-unit bridge between speech encoder and text decoder
LanguageCoverage: LibriSpeech; MuST-C; unpaired speech and text
MainFinding: Strong evidence that speech-text coupling improves ASR and ST beyond speech-only pretraining.
Limitations: Still evaluated mostly on mainstream benchmarks.
UseInReview: Use to justify later speech-text and SpeechLM sections.

Title: SpeechLM: Enhanced Speech Pre-Training With Unpaired Textual Data
MethodOrContribution: Align speech and text using unified discrete representations and unpaired text
MainFinding: Clear bridge from speech SSL to true speech-language pretraining.
Limitations: Low-resource ASR evidence is still indirect; more transfer validation is needed.
UseInReview: Use in the speech-language integration subsection.

Title: DinoSR: Self-Distillation and Online Clustering for Self-supervised Speech Representation Learning
MethodOrContribution: Combine self-distillation, MLM, and online clustering for speech SSL
MainFinding: Strong late-stage SSL paper showing that the encoder line was still improving after HuBERT and WavLM.
Limitations: Less central to multilingual low-resource transfer than XLS-R or MMS.
UseInReview: Use as evidence that SSL encoder innovation did not stop in 2021 to 2022.

Title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
MethodOrContribution: Web-scale weak supervision over audio-transcript pairs
MainFinding: Perhaps the clearest practical reset of the low-resource baseline through large-scale weak supervision and robust zero- and few-shot transfer.
Limitations: Transcription style normalization and data provenance remain important caveats.
UseInReview: Core anchor for the weak-supervision subsection.

Title: Google USM: Scaling Automatic Speech Recognition Beyond 100 Languages
MethodOrContribution: Massive multilingual encoder pretraining plus speech-text modality matching
LanguageCoverage: 12M hours speech; 28B text sentences; 300+ languages; 100+ ASR languages
MainFinding: High-value scaling reference showing that very large multilingual pretraining can compete with or exceed Whisper on many languages.
Limitations: Preprint or product-adjacent release rather than a mature peer-reviewed archive paper.
UseInReview: Use as a watchlist anchor for industrial-scale multilingual ASR.

Title: Scaling Speech Technology to 1,000+ Languages
MethodOrContribution: Massively multilingual speech recognition, identification, and alignment at unprecedented language count
MainFinding: Strongest public evidence that language coverage itself became a first-order foundation-model variable.
Limitations: Breadth does not automatically imply robustness on every tail language or domain.
UseInReview: Core anchor for expanded language coverage.

Title: Joint speech and text machine translation for up to 100 languages
MethodOrContribution: Unified speech and text multitask model covering S2S, S2T, T2S, T2T, and ASR
Evaluation: WER; translation quality; multilingual task metrics
MainFinding: The clearest peer-reviewed statement of speech-text foundation modeling beyond plain ASR, with ASR as one supported task.
Limitations: Translation-centric framing means low-resource ASR analysis still needs external validation papers.
UseInReview: Use as the multimodal foundation-model anchor.

Title: Qwen2-Audio Technical Report
MethodOrContribution: Instruction-following audio-language model with voice chat and audio analysis modes
LanguageCoverage: General audio and speech instruction data
MainFinding: Valuable frontier reference for speech-LLM capability, especially for the review's LLM-assisted section.
Limitations: Not a dedicated low-resource ASR paper and not peer reviewed in a major venue.
UseInReview: Use in the future-directions and SpeechLM frontier section.

Title: Evaluating Speech Foundation Models for Automatic Speech Recognition in the Low-Resource Kanyen'keha Language
MethodOrContribution: Systematic comparison of wav2vec2, HuBERT, WavLM, data2vec, and Whisper under cross-lingual transfer plus TTS augmentation and LM fusion
MainFinding: One of the most valuable direct RQ2 papers: SFMs beat conventional hybrids, but low-resource success still depends on adaptation choices and data augmentation.
Limitations: Single-language case study; external generalization still limited.
UseInReview: Use as a case box proving that foundation models help without solving the problem.

Title: Towards large-scale speech foundation models for a low-resource minority language
MethodOrContribution: Build language-specific foundation models from large unlabeled archival audio
MainFinding: Important corrective paper showing that low-resource can still permit foundation modeling if unlabeled archives are recoverable.
Limitations: Strong language-specific case, but not a general multilingual model.
UseInReview: Use to argue for community- and archive-driven foundation modeling.

Title: Making LLMs Better Many-to-Many Speech-to-Text Translators with Curriculum Learning
MethodOrContribution: Three-stage curriculum for adapting multilingual LLMs to speech-to-text translation
MainFinding: Strong evidence that LLM-centric speech systems can leverage curriculum and MT priors in low-resource settings.
Limitations: More S2TT than ASR; should support future-direction claims, not replace ASR anchors.
UseInReview: Use in SpeechLM and LLM-assisted future work discussion.

Title: OpusLM: A Family of Open Unified Speech Language Models
MethodOrContribution: Open decoder-style SpeechLM family up to 7B with transparent training logs, code, and checkpoints
MainFinding: High-value open reference showing scaling laws and competitive open SpeechLM performance.
Limitations: Still early; low-resource ASR evidence is promising but not yet definitive.
UseInReview: Use as an open-model counterpoint to proprietary or industrial systems.

Title: Omnilingual ASR: Open-Source Multilingual Speech Recognition for 1600+ Languages
MethodOrContribution: Community-extensible multilingual ASR suite for 1600+ languages
MainFinding: One of the most important 2025 watchlist items because it pushes public multilingual ASR scale far beyond MMS-era coverage and explicitly invites community extension.
Limitations: Release-page or preprint stage; peer-reviewed validation not yet settled.
UseInReview: Use as a 2025 watchlist anchor in the future agenda.

Title: SLAM-LLM: A Modular, Open-Source Multimodal Large Language Model Framework and Best Practice for Speech, Language, Audio and Music Processing
MethodOrContribution: Modular framework with speech encoders, projectors, LLMs, PEFT, and ASR recipes
MainFinding: Important because it lowers the barrier to reproducible SpeechLM experimentation and LLM-based ASR recipes.
Limitations: Framework paper rather than a single canonical model; peer-reviewed status still needs confirmation.
UseInReview: Use in future agenda and reproducibility/tooling discussion.

Title: LoASR-Bench: Evaluating Large Speech Language Models on Low-Resource Automatic Speech Recognition Across Language Families
MethodOrContribution: Dedicated benchmark for SpeechLMs on low-resource ASR across language families
MainFinding: This is the most directly useful 2026 watchlist item for RQ2 because it tests whether SpeechLM-era claims actually survive on low-resource ASR.
Limitations: Preprint only; benchmark uptake and protocol stability still need validation.
UseInReview: Use in watchlist and future work and to motivate stronger evaluation requirements.
